title: Construction of constructible truncations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y$ be a
finite-type $k$-scheme, where
finite type is the scheme
condition used throughout. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For $\Lambda=E$, let
$D^b_c(Y,E)$ be the
rationalized
category obtained
from integral complexes whose finite-level reductions satisfy the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use the
common finite-stage
coefficient construction. The symbols $\mathcal H^r$ denote the
cohomology sheaves of a
derived complex. Let $m,i\in\mathbf Z$.
There are truncation functors

$$
\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).
$$

At a common finite coefficient field they are the
standard truncations of the
constructible derived category; they commute with finite scalar extension and
with the transitions of the coefficient tower.
For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, these truncations, their natural maps, and the
distinguished truncation triangles satisfy the axioms of a
bounded t-structure. For
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define its cohomology functors by

$$
\mathcal H^i(K)=\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K\bigr)[i].
$$

For every scheme automorphism $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$, the
derived pullback $Lh^*$
commutes with the truncations and with $\mathcal H^i$.

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *Verification of the operations and cohomological interfaces* of the source.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and $\mathcal C_A=D^b_c(Y,A)$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is noetherian and quasi-compact: a field has just the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to the same morphism; its only fibre is $Y$, so $Y$ is finite-dimensional. Finally $\ell$ is a unit in $k$ because $\ell\ne p$, and its image is a unit in each local ring of $Y$. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] now hold. Its explicit comparison clause identifies the full subcategory of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with the completed bounded constructible category used by the integral and localized t-structure theorems, with the same ring sheaf and reduction functors. In particular the compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform local models required there are supplied by this cited theorem; they are not inferred merely from the notation $D^b_c$.

source.place: Proof, integral-category passage; geometric hypotheses and identification of integral conventions

proof.text: At a torsion coefficient level, use the standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Canonical upper truncation replaces the cutoff term by a kernel and canonical lower truncation replaces its cutoff term by a cokernel, as in Stacks Tag 0118 (homology-section-truncations). Their surviving cohomology sheaves are exactly the original ones and the other cohomology sheaves are zero; the upper calculation is [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], and the lower calculation follows directly by taking $\operatorname{coker}d^{m-1}$ in degree $m$. Thus boundedness and the finite partitions in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] survive truncation. The standard triangles restrict to this full triangulated subcategory. At the integral stage, apply [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] after step 1: it supplies the bounded t-structure, both ambient canonical truncation restrictions, their maps and their distinguished triangles on all of $\mathcal C_A$. This application uses no flat-cohomology assumption. It also does not identify the reductions of an arbitrary integral truncation with the truncations of the reductions; such an identification has the extra Tor hypothesis recorded in the cited integral theorem.

source.place: Proof, first four sentences: finite and integral truncations; corrected use of ambient integral truncations

proof.text: Use the raw scalar localization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so that $\mathcal C_E=\mathcal C_A[1/\varpi_E]$ has the same objects and localized Hom groups; no idempotent completion is involved. By step 1 the categories and localization functor are exactly those in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. That theorem gives the bounded t-structure on $\mathcal C_E$, its natural truncation comparisons $\tau_E^{\le m}QK\cong Q\tau_A^{\le m}K$ and $\tau_E^{\ge m}QK\cong Q\tau_A^{\ge m}K$, and t-exactness of $Q$. The canonical maps and triangles are the images of the integral ones. This identifies the finite coefficient-field t-structure with the rational standard pair of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure].

Let $E\subset L$ be finite coefficient fields, and put $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is finite free over $R$ and, for a derived-complete $K$, the actual integral scalar extension is naturally $K\otimes_R^L S$. Choose an $R$-basis of $S$ solely to check exactness: after forgetting the $S$-action, tensoring any module sheaf with $S$ is a finite direct sum of copies of that module sheaf. Finite direct sums preserve kernels and cokernels, so this tensor functor is exact. Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to obtain $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_R^L S)\cong\mathcal H^r(K)\otimes_R S$ naturally. It preserves both cohomological half-categories, and [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] supplies membership in the target integral category. Hence integral scalar extension is t-exact; after localization the same is true of $-\otimes_E L$, since the rational halves are the isomorphism closures of integral halves. This rational functor is triangulated by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]. Apply it to a truncation triangle: its end terms have degrees $\le m$ and $\ge m+1$. The characterization of canonical truncation triangles in [def-weil-t-structure] identifies that image triangle with the target truncation triangle, yielding natural isomorphisms $T_{L/E}\tau_E^{\le m}\cong\tau_L^{\le m}T_{L/E}$ and $T_{L/E}\tau_E^{\ge m}\cong\tau_L^{\ge m}T_{L/E}$, compatible with the maps. The identity and composition comparisons of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition] respect these isomorphisms: both composites are the canonical comparison with the same truncation maps. Thus compatibility includes the whole directed coefficient-field tower. Here these transitions are finite field extensions, not non-flat reductions $A/\varpi^{n+1}\to A/\varpi^n$.

source.place: Proof, scalar-extension and coefficient-tower compatibility; exactness and t-exactness supplied explicitly

proof.text: In the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], define $\tau^{\le m}(E,K)=(E,\tau_E^{\le m}K)$ and likewise $\tau^{\ge m}(E,K)=(E,\tau_E^{\ge m}K)$. For a morphism represented by $u:K\otimes_E L\to K'\otimes_{E'}L$, apply $\tau_L^{\le m}$ and use step 4's comparisons to regard its source and target as scalar extensions of $\tau_E^{\le m}K$ and $\tau_{E'}^{\le m}K'$; use the analogous rule for $\tau^{\ge m}$. If two representatives agree over a larger field, their truncations agree there by naturality and composition compatibility from step 4. Thus these rules define functors; identities and compositions are checked on representatives over one common field. Define their maps and triangles by the finite-stage maps and triangles. Step 4 makes those independent of enlargement too, and the triangles are distinguished by the common-stage definition. This constructs the requested truncations with every common finite-field presentation.

source.place: Proof, descent of truncation functors and triangles to the common-stage category

proof.text: For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, take the two standard classes of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], namely objects isomorphic to finite-stage nonpositive or nonnegative objects. Shifting such a representative proves the two shift inclusions in [def-weil-t-structure]. For orthogonality, replace the source and target by representatives in degrees $\le0$ and $\ge1$, and extend both to one common field. By step 4 these bounds persist under every further field extension. The finite-stage Hom group is therefore zero at every such stage, and its directed colimit, the Hom group of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], is zero. The triangle constructed in step 5 has its end terms in the required halves, giving the truncation axiom. Finally an object $(E,K)$ has upper and lower bounds already over $E$ by step 3; the same bounds work in the common-stage category. This proves all t-structure axioms and boundedness, rather than assuming that functorial descent alone proves them.

source.place: Proof, bounded t-structure at algebraically closed coefficients

proof.text: For either field stage define $\mathcal H^i$ to be the composite $K\mapsto(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}K)[i]$ displayed in the statement. The truncation maps are functorial, so this is a functor. Its value lies in the heart: before shifting it has only degree $i$, and the cohomological shift $[i]$ moves that degree to zero. At the integral and torsion stages it is the degree-$i$ cohomology sheaf of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], placed in degree zero, by the kernel/image descriptions; at a field stage it is its rationalized or common-stage heart object. Thus no identification of an abstract rational heart with an ambient category of $E$-sheaves is assumed.

source.place: Proof, displayed definition of cohomology functors

proof.text: Let $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme automorphism. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], its inverse image is relabelling the small pro-etale site by $U\to Y\mapsto U\xrightarrow{}Y\xrightarrow{h}Y$, an exact equivalence preserving all limits and the coefficient maps. On completed coefficient sheaves it therefore identifies $h^{-1}R$ with $R$ by taking the limit of the compatible finite coefficient identifications. This induces an exact equivalence on module sheaves and, termwise, on complexes. It preserves kernels, images and their quotients by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], so $\mathcal H^r(h^{-1}K)\cong h^{-1}\mathcal H^r(K)$. The tensor comparison of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] identifies the pulled-back finite reduction with the finite reduction of the pulled-back complex. If $P$ is K-flat and $C$ is acyclic on the target, then $h^{-1}P\otimes C\cong h^{-1}(P\otimes h_*C)$ by the tensor comparison and the inverse equivalence. Exactness makes $h_*C$ acyclic; K-flatness makes $P\otimes h_*C$ acyclic; exactness again makes its inverse image acyclic. Thus $h^{-1}P$ is K-flat. It preserves countable products and cones termwise. The products compute derived products by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence](2). Use the strict reduction-tower cone in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], which is the integral operation named by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Applying the equivalence to this cone identifies, naturally and with its projections, the completed pullback $Lh^*K$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with $h^{-1}K$ for derived-complete $K$: the two product maps are both $(x_n)\mapsto(x_n-t_nx_{n+1})$, and the identification of their shifted cones is termwise. Here the canonical completion map is invertible by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] with $L=E$, and [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] supplies derived completeness. This uses the functorial strict model, not a claimed uniqueness of maps between abstract Roos triangles. Membership in the target integral category is supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](1). Termwise inverse image commutes with the cohomological shift (including the sign of the differential) and with the cone matrix of any chain map, so its derived functor preserves distinguished triangles. Its identified integral restriction is coefficient-linear, and therefore preserves the images of these triangles under scalar localization. Thus $Lh^*$ is triangulated and t-exact on the integral category and its rationalization: it preserves the cohomological bounds of steps 2 and 3. For every cutoff $m$, applying it to $\tau^{\le m}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge m+1}K$ gives a distinguished triangle whose end terms have bounds $\le m$ and $\ge m+1$. The characterization in [def-weil-t-structure] identifies these terms with the canonical truncations of $Lh^*K$, compatibly with the maps to and from $Lh^*K$. The same characterization for morphisms gives naturality, so both natural truncation comparisons hold at $E$.

source.place: Proof, automorphism compatibility; exact module equivalence and t-exactness replace the invalid triangulated-exactness inference

proof.text: Write $F_E=Lh_E^*$ and $T_{L/E}=-\otimes_E L$. For either truncation $\tau_E$ at the fixed cutoff, let $\alpha_E:F_E\tau_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_EF_E$ be the natural comparison from step 8. For an integral representative $K$, apply the first comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] to $f=h$; its hypotheses hold by step 1 and step 8. Localizing this integral isomorphism gives $\beta_{L/E}:T_{L/E}F_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_LT_{L/E}$. On a rational morphism $u\otimes a$, with $u$ integral and $a\in E$, its naturality square is the integral square for $u$ multiplied by $a$: both functors are coefficient-linear and the scalar-extension morphism rule is the one in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Every element of a localized Hom group is a finite sum $\sum_j u_j\otimes a_j$. Choose $N\ge0$ with $b_j=\varpi_E^N a_j\in\mathcal O_E$ for all $j$; this sum equals $(\sum_j b_j u_j)\otimes\varpi_E^{-N}$, so the preceding square calculation covers every rational morphism. Hence $\beta$ is natural on every rational morphism, not only on integral ones. The integral identity and field-tower coherence equalities in the cited comparison remain equalities after localization, so $\beta$ is compatible with identity and composite extensions. Combine $\beta$, the scalar/truncation comparisons of step 4 and $T_{L/E}\alpha_E$ to compare $F_L\tau_LT_{L/E}K$ with $\tau_LF_LT_{L/E}K$. This comparison and $\alpha_L(T_{L/E}K)$ preserve the canonical truncation maps into or out of $F_LT_{L/E}K$. They agree by the characterization of truncation triangles in [def-weil-t-structure]. For a morphism represented by $u:T_{L/E}K\to T_{L/E'}K'$ at a common field $L$, use these identifications to write the comparison square as the naturality square of $\alpha_L$ for $u$, which commutes. If $u$ and $u'$ represent the same morphism, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] says they agree over a further common field $M$; their two squares then agree over $M$ by the established extension compatibility, and hence represent the same square in the colimit. The components represented by $\alpha_E(K)$ therefore give a natural isomorphism in the common-stage category, whose inverse is represented by $\alpha_E(K)^{-1}$. This is a comparison for the actual pullback on morphisms specified by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], whose morphism rule uses exactly $\beta$. The two choices $\tau^{\le m}$ and $\tau^{\ge m}$ give both required comparisons. Finally $Lh^*$ commutes with shifts by the termwise model of step 8 and its scalar and common-stage morphism rules. For $\Lambda=E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, their composition is the natural isomorphism $Lh^*((\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}K)[i])\cong(\tau^{\ge i}Lh^*\tau^{\le i}K)[i]\cong(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}Lh^*K)[i]$, which is precisely $Lh^*\mathcal H^i(K)\cong\mathcal H^i(Lh^*K)$.

split_report.summary: Split into nine steps with no new nodes. Kept the statement. Reused the exact existing integral-category comparison, integral and localized bounded t-structures, and finite-free completed scalar comparison. Proved scalar t-exactness and finite-stage descent explicitly, checked the common-stage t-structure axioms, and proved automorphism t-exactness by exact module transport and the strict completion cone. Corrected the imported proof assertions that truncation is triangulated, that arbitrary reduction commutes with truncation, and that triangulated exactness implies truncation compatibility. Tagged project Lean omits the required E-stage, so no attachment. Independent second reading added the strict integral-operation definition citation, spelled out K-flatness and triangulatedness of automorphism transport, and expanded descent of the natural comparisons on morphism representatives. All dependency statements remain unchanged; citations now include the complete used statements.
